Not hard to use, and good exercise. - The Easy Go Washing Wand comes in a small box and in 4 pieces. The washer-part can be connected to any of the 2 extensions or directly to the handle itself for a shorter version or a smaller wash. But with the standard 5 gallon plastic bucket filled with soapy water, which can splash up and be messy, the full assembly keeps you clear of the washing process. It's not hard to push and pull the washer through the clothes, and the wash goes around as you push it down and other parts of the wash load are pushed up. I tried it on a bunch of really dirty, greasy things and in only a minute the water was brown as a sign it was working. The washer-head submerges and vents some of the water you're pushing down into so the clothes get the jet-action of the soapy water going through them. In another 5 gallon bucket filled with the rinse water, the same action with the washer-assembly removes the soapy water. A wringer comes in handy, but the hardest part, which is the agitation of the clothes in the wash-water is taken care of and much simplified by this fantastic plastic washer thing.
It looks unbreakable, and good for a lot of washing!

Expensive but heavy duty paper type product - Chemex has a couple of these white coffee filters on the market; this one lists around 11 bucks; there is an almost identical one that lists at 9 bucks through Amazon too. I have both products (wanted to see what the difference was). I don't see any major (or minor) differences, so first, buy the cheaper one (my advice). As to the product, they really are much heavier than the typical coffee filters you buy--even the "better" brands. One thing though, these are kind of weird. You get them, and they are folded in four sections. You can use them on a regular coffee machine (cone type), but they are specifically designed for the glass chemex glass decanters. What's strange is you are directed to unfold one portion (of the folded pieces) and put the other three sides toward the decanter pouring opening. In essence you have three sides touching the glass on one side and one side touching the glass on the other side where is all fits into the cone (or rounded opening). So why have three sides to filter when the other side is just one layer thick? It's hard to explain, and other reviewers have tried; don't let that discourage you though, it really is a great product, and it (these heavy filters) is the main reason Chemex glass decanters produce such superior coffee (well, that plus the fact that you control the temperature of the water going through your coffee grounds). Hope this helps. Update: The difference between the FC-100 and the FS-100 is this one is a CONE and the other one is just a sheet of paper folded into quarters (a reqular sheet of paper folded twice). The cone fits a little better into the Chemex in my opinion. Prices fluctuate, so keep that in mind.

The TDS levels are higher than my tap water - We bought a house that was five years old and came with the refrigerator. I took the reading of the filtered refrigerator water, the tap at kitchen sink, the bathroom faucet and bottled water. The refrigerator, the kitchen, & the bathroom all read 157 ppm and the bottled water reading was 30 ppm, so this told me I needed to replace the filter.

I ordered this filter when it arrived I installed it and ran the refrigerator water dispenser the 3 mins per instructions plus an additional 3 mins. I took the first reading and it was at 776 ppm!! I ran the water an additional 5 mins and it dropped to 237 ppm. A week later it registers 172 ppm, so I call Frigidaire to find out if there is an explanation to which they had none and told me that maybe a got a bad one and that I should contact Amazon for and exchange, which I did and as always Amazon was very helpful and sent me a replacement. The new one...... it started out with a 227 reading it is now (after being installed 8 days) reading 146 ppm with my tap at 158 ppm.

Get a transparent hose for easier drainage troubleshooting - I have done a lot of dishwasher troubleshooting as a manager of rental properties. Most dishwasher drain hoses I encounter are somewhat transparent. I can see water and debris flowing through them and can see accumulated debris. This is useful when troubleshooting a drainage issue or investigating a possible clog. While not essential, since transparent hoses are so readily available, why not get one of those instead of this opaque one? The transparent ones are the hazy white-colored one that allows light through. For the prior drainage issue I dealt with I was able to see the clog in the drainage hose, which I would not have been able to do if this opaque hose was installed.

This product does not come with clamps, which you should be using to secure the ends in place. If you are replacing a drain hose, then you already have the clamps.

Dishwasher drain hoses are not all the same size. There are common sizes of the end connectors, but this is not a universal part, and you need to get one that can connect to both your dishwasher and your garbage disposal. Other drain hoses have can be adjusted to fit the various sizes of holes, but this product is only one size.
